domains.name: Sales Prompts
domains.intro: Working templates for discovery, outreach, and objection handling. Replace the {PLACEHOLDERS}, paste your own source material where indicated, and keep the output format lines, they are what make results consistent.

domains.name: Marketing Prompts
domains.intro: Templates for briefs, content, and campaign planning. Feed them real positioning and real audience data, the output quality tracks the input quality almost linearly.

domains.name: Finance Prompts
domains.intro: Templates for analysis narratives and board communication. These draft and structure; the numbers and the judgment remain yours, and outputs are not financial advice.

domains.name: Coding Prompts
domains.intro: Templates for review, debugging, and testing. Paste real code and real errors; every output should be verified by running it.

domains.name: HR Prompts
domains.intro: Templates for hiring and feedback work. AI-assisted employment decisions carry legal exposure (see the hiring discrimination cases in the AI Lawsuit Tracker); these templates draft documents for human review, they do not screen or rank people.

domains.name: Cybersecurity Prompts
domains.intro: Templates for triage, reporting, and policy review. Defensive work only; never paste live credentials, secrets, or regulated personal data into a prompt.

domains.name: Healthcare Prompts
domains.intro: Templates for administrative and communication work in healthcare settings. None of these produce clinical guidance, and no patient identifiers should ever be pasted into a prompt; HIPAA applies to AI tools like any other system.

domains.name: Education Prompts
domains.intro: Templates for lesson design, rubrics, and differentiation. The teacher remains the judge of accuracy and fit; never paste student names or records into a prompt.

techniques.name: Zero-Shot Prompting
techniques.what: Asking the model to do a task with a direct instruction and no examples, relying entirely on what it learned in training.

techniques.name: Few-Shot Prompting
techniques.what: Showing the model two to five worked examples of the task inside the prompt so it infers the pattern before doing yours.

techniques.name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
techniques.what: Prompting the model to reason step by step before giving its answer, either by showing worked reasoning in examples or simply instructing it to think through the problem first.

techniques.name: Self-Consistency
techniques.what: Running the same reasoning prompt several times with sampling enabled and taking the majority answer across the runs.

techniques.name: ReAct (Reason + Act)
techniques.what: Interleaving reasoning steps with tool calls, the model thinks, acts (searches, runs code, queries an API), observes the result, and reasons again until it can answer.

techniques.name: Tree of Thoughts
techniques.what: Having the model explore several reasoning branches, evaluate which look promising, and backtrack from dead ends, search over thoughts instead of one linear chain.

techniques.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
techniques.what: Fetching relevant documents at question time and placing them in the prompt so the model answers from your sources instead of memory.

techniques.name: Prompt Chaining
techniques.what: Splitting a complex job into a sequence of smaller prompts where each step's output becomes the next step's input.

techniques.name: Role Prompting
techniques.what: Assigning the model a persona or professional role, you are an experienced financial auditor, before the task.

techniques.name: Meta Prompting
techniques.what: Using a model to write, critique, or refine prompts, describing the task and letting the model draft the instructions another run will follow.

sources_note: Technique pages draw on the openly licensed prompt engineering literature, principally the DAIR.AI Prompt Engineering Guide (MIT) and the original papers each page cites; templates are original to this site.
learning_path: If you are new, the order matters less than the habit: start with zero-shot and learn to specify what done looks like, add few-shot when the model keeps missing your format, add chain-of-thought when problems have steps, and treat everything after that as situational tooling, self-consistency for high-stakes answers, chaining for pipelines, RAG for grounding, ReAct when tools enter. The techniques compound: a production prompt is usually three of them at once. And the field's direction is worth knowing as you learn: reasoning models are absorbing chain-of-thought and tree search into the model itself, so the durable human skills are the ones models cannot absorb, knowing your task, your data, your definition of good, and writing them down precisely.

items.claim: Adding emotionally charged phrases to prompts, a technique its authors called EmotionPrompt, raised relative performance by 8 percent on instruction induction tasks and 115 percent on BIG-Bench in their tests.
items.source_title: Large Language Models Understand and Can be Enhanced by Emotional Stimuli, arXiv

items.claim: Meta prompting, in which a single task agnostic prompt structures how a model approaches problems, let a Qwen 72B model reach 46.3 percent on MATH and 83.5 percent on GSM8K in its authors' evaluation.
Anthropic describes context engineering as curating the smallest set of high value information a model sees at inference time, the discipline that has grown out of prompt engineering for agents.
items.source_title: Anthropic engineering, Effective context engineering for AI agents
